owner.name: Samuel Flg
owner.one_liner: Samuel builds interfaces where the page itself is the agent.

offerings.title: A website that is the agent
offerings.what: An interface that is the agent itself, not a page with a chat box beside it. One conversation, one look.
offerings.for_whom: Studios and small teams who want a site that answers instead of a brochure.
offerings.example: A studio owner asks what is possible; the surface answers in a few short lines and asks one real question back.

offerings.title: A version of one person
offerings.what: The same behaviour, filled with that person's words and boundaries.
offerings.for_whom: Someone who wants an agent that speaks as them and is unsure what that would take.
offerings.example: Three things you would say at a first meeting, and one thing you would never say.

offerings.title: An interface for a team's knowledge
offerings.what: An interface for an internal knowledge team, built around retrieval first and surface second.
offerings.for_whom: A company evaluating an interface for its internal knowledge team.
offerings.example: Eight people, four documents and a wiki. The agent starts by asking for three real questions the team asked last week.

approach.point: Read first, draw second, structure third, build last.
Search what already exists before building anything new.
Measure the risky assumption before building on it.
Text first; voice comes later and starts on click.
Answer fast in front; slower agents work behind and do not interrupt.
The agent can ask what it should look like, and the page changes live.
Not patronising: the page never tells the visitor what to do.

faq.a: An interface that is the agent itself, not a page with a chat window next to it.
No. A chatbot is something a page has. Here the page is the agent, and it changes while you talk to it.

faq.q: Can it be built for me or my team?
faq.a: That is what it is for. The shape depends on what the interface has to do, not on a fixed package.
That is a deployment question. The build supports it; the policy is the client's.
It answers from what is in the current conversation, not from memory. It can shape an answer around what you say, not recall you later.
There is no price list here yet. Samuel quotes after he has heard what you actually need.

open_questions_for_samuel.question: How should a visitor reach you? The knowledge base has contact.method and contact.text as null, so the agent can only say the way is not here yet.
open_questions_for_samuel.context: Owner decision 5 allows the agent to pass contact on. No route (address, form, booking link) is confirmed anywhere in the sources.

open_questions_for_samuel.question: May the agent accept a visitor's own address in the chat and forward it to you — and is that forwarding actually built?
open_questions_for_samuel.context: The hurried-decider pathway promises it. Nothing in src/ implements forwarding.

open_questions_for_samuel.question: Is 'I do not quote. Samuel does, after he has heard what you actually need.' the approved pricing stance, or should pricing stay entirely out of the conversation?
open_questions_for_samuel.context: pricing.stance is null until you decide.

open_questions_for_samuel.question: May the agent say anything about timelines or availability?
open_questions_for_samuel.context: The pathway offers 'a thin one' within a week. That is a promise the agent cannot verify today.

open_questions_for_samuel.question: Which offerings may be named publicly: website, person, team, and what about company-wide builds?
open_questions_for_samuel.context: The sketch lists website, person, team and company; the pathways only show a website, a person and a team case.

open_questions_for_samuel.question: Which projects may appear as public references? None are approved yet, so the agent must not present any.
open_questions_for_samuel.context: No reference is verifiable from these sources. Client and employer work is excluded by the privacy rule.

open_questions_for_samuel.question: Which role label do you want in public: 'AI engineer', 'builder', or something else?
open_questions_for_samuel.context: The knowledge base currently says 'Builds Human-Agent Interfaces' from the vision document.

open_questions_for_samuel.question: Is English the only public language, or should the agent answer in German too?
open_questions_for_samuel.context: English is decided for voice and text; German is parked as a later feature.
